A university course registration system manages student enrollments. All students must register for a minimum of 12 credits. Undergraduate students must select one 100-level Core course, while Graduate students must select a 500-level Seminar. Many courses have prerequisites; for example, 'Advanced AI' requires both 'Intro to AI' and 'Linear Algebra'. Some courses are mutually exclusive, like 'Statistics for Biology' and 'Statistics for Business'. The 'Robotics Lab' course is an optional elective with a hard enrollment cap of 20 students. Finally, the 'Thesis Defense' module is only available to students who have completed 60 credits and passed their 'Dissertation Proposal' review.

test_results.output:
'''uvl
features
    'PC Configurator Tool'
        alternative
            'CPU Choice' {cpu}
                mandatory
                    'Intel' | 'AMD'
        mandatory
            'Motherboard Socket' {socket}
                alternative
                    'LGA 1700'
                    'AM5'
        mandatory
            'Chipset' {chipset}
                alternative
                    'Z790'
        optional
            'High-end GPU' {gpu}
                mandatory
                    'RTX 4090'
        optional
            'Power Supply Requirement' {psu}
                alternative
                    '850W'
                    '1200W'
        mandatory
            'GPU Physical Length' {length}
                alternative
                    '350mm'
        mandatory
            'Case Form Factor' {case}
                alternative
                    'ATX'
                    'Micro-ATX'
        optional
            'Large Air Cooler Height' {coolersize}

constraints
    CaseFormFactor(Atx) => LargeAirCoolerHeightLessThan(CPU_Cooler_Clearance)
    CaseFormFactor(MicroATX) => LargeAirCoolerHeightGreaterThan(Case_CPU_Cooler_Clearance)

'''
test_results.text: A PC configurator tool guides users. The choice of CPU (e.g., Intel vs. AMD) dictates the required motherboard socket (e.g., LGA 1700 vs. AM5). The motherboard chipset (e.g., Z790) then determines the supported RAM type (DDR4 or DDR5). A high-end GPU (e.g., RTX 4090) has a minimum power requirement, constraining the choice of Power Supply (PSU) to 850W or higher. The GPU's physical length (e.g., 350mm) must also be compatible with the case's maximum GPU clearance. Finally, the case (e.g., ATX, Micro-ATX) must match the motherboard's form factor, and an optional large air cooler's height must be less than the case's CPU cooler clearance.

test_results.output:
'''uvl
features
    CI_CD_system {abstract}
        mandatory
            Build
            Unit_Test

        optional
            Staging {after(Unit_Test)}

        optional
            Production
                mandatory
                    Staging
                mandatory
                    Integration_Test
                mandatory
                    Security_Scan
                optional
                    Blue_Green_strategy
                        mandatory
                            Monitoring {with(Rollback)}
                optional
                    Canary_strategy
                        mandatory
                            Hotfix_pipeline
                                mandatory
                                    Manual_QA_Approval
                                    mandatory
                                        Security_Scan
                        mandatory
                            Hotfix_pipeline
                                mandatory
                                    Manual_QA_Approval
                                    mandatory
                                        Security_Scan

constraints
    Hotfix_pipeline_or_Blue_Green_strategy
        alternative
            Hotfix_pipeline
            Blue_Green_strategy

'''
test_results.text: A CI/CD system defines deployment pipelines. All pipelines must run 'Build' and 'Unit Test' stages. A 'Staging' deployment is mandatory and can only run after 'Unit Test' passes. The 'Production' deployment requires the 'Staging' deployment to succeed, and also requires both 'Integration Test' and 'Security Scan' to pass. For 'Production', the user can select either a 'Blue/Green' or 'Canary' strategy. Choosing 'Canary' automatically adds a 'Monitoring' stage with a 'Rollback' trigger. Choosing 'Blue/Green' requires double the infrastructure resources during the swap. A separate 'Hotfix' pipeline can bypass 'Staging' and 'Integration Test', but requires a 'Manual QA Approval' step and must still pass the 'Security Scan'.

A smart home automation system links devices based on rules. A rule has triggers, optional conditions, and actions. Rules must have priorities to resolve conflicts: the 'Movie Mode' scene (sets lights to 10%) must block the 'Morning' scene (sets lights to 100%) from running. Safety constraints are critical: the 'Smart Oven' action is disabled if 'Home Status' is 'Away'. Also, the 'Air Conditioner' action is dynamically disabled if any 'Window Sensor' reports 'Open' and only re-enables 5 minutes after all windows are closed.
